newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares to rise after profit-taking bout.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares to rise after profit-taking bout.

text.p: Belgian shares suffered profit-taking on Wednesday after recent bull runs, but dealers expected shares to push higher after some days of profit-taking because good economic fundamentals remained in place.
"It's just a small blip, we'll see some more profit-taking then we will go higher again because the economic picture is positive," said one trader.
The Brussels blue-chip Bel-20 index dipped 0.46 percent, or 10.16 points, to close at 2,210.16, with a modest 2.8 billion francs volume worth of Belgian shares traded.
"It's breathing time for the Bel-20. We need it after recent jumps," said another trader.
Belgian stocks were also undermined by falls in European markets, and a weaker Dow Jones opening.
"Click funds are still coming onto the market and there is still some aggressive buying out there, so I'm not worried that we're about to see a correction," a trader said.

Some shares in the banking sector suffered from profit-taking after record rises earlier in the week, fuelled by speculation of a possible merger between Belgium's largest bank Generale Bank and bank BBL.
Generale Bank dropped 2.14 percent to 13,700 francs and rival bank Kredietbank fell 1.12 percent to 13,200.

But BBL managed to climb higher, closing up 0.84 percent at 8,360 francs and financial group Fortis AG closed up 1.26 percent at 6,450 francs as institutionals continued to pour into the banking sector.
Elsewhere pharmaceutical and drugs group UCB closed up 1.27 percent at 95,800 francs, catching up after lagging recent market rises.
